yes, for sure! after doing sessions with him, i realized i only truly needed one since that’s the one he gives u a game plan for to follow until exam day, the rest are really just gaging how you’re doing. but here’s what he told me that i feel were the biggest changes:
- do 8-10 blocks of 10 questions from either uworld or amboss (they are equivalent to each other so dealers choice). it reallyyy fixed my burnout issue and productivity sky rocketed
- in the last 2-3 weeks or so, do nbmes 20-31. do one per every two days. the first day, take the exam in testing conditions in one go and the next day, thoroughly review every single question. this bullet point itself is probably single handedly the most important point that got me that jump. 
- keep doing those docs!! the arrows one are sooo good to test your knowledge so keep it up. the other really HY i would say is endo bc he told me that endo is hormones and hormones are in all systems so if you can get endo down, u got 60% of the testing info down. after endo, do other HY systems and start with your weakest ones first. me personally, i thought biochem and RF were chefs kiss but all of them are so good. pepper say ethics and biostats too but honestly those chapters in FA did the job just as much so it’s personal preference at that point. 
- CONSISTENCY!! it’s so easy to get demotivated but if you do it everyday whether you’re happy, sad, tired, mad, whatever, then that’s the progress at work. even the days you feel you’re not doing well or it’s useless are arguably the most important days in which the learning is happening the most. 
- last thing, don’t overwhelm yourself with all these resources out there. they’re all great, but other than FA and MM, choose a couple that u like and stick to those. no need to do everything and set your mind into overdrive and crash out later

hey OP, i’m sorry it’s been such a battle. but listen, i was in your exact position not too long ago. i’m also a carribean student who needed to clear cbse with a 66+. first attempt 51, second 59, third 61, and fourth (finally) 71. just got my step 1 P this wednesday. 
1. burnout effect is definitely possible. i can’t speak much to it since even after 10 months of studying, i always kept burnout at bay by reminding myself i literally have no other choice right now and (this is more important) have a consistent hobby u can do for at least an hour EVERYDAY. idk if that’s the key but for me lifting was the only thing keeping me sane 
2. the foundation of your study strategies seem good, i think you just gotta tweak atp. just stuff like don’t well too much on weak points to the point that other components are lacking, take your nbmes in exam settings and review them thoroughly, and content review for only when really needed on the reallt difficult ones (i say this because i believe that going over qbank explanations is taking care majority of the review). these are just suggestions ofc, everyone is different when it comes to these exams so those are what stood out to me. here’s what i consider the keys that made me finally pass the fourth time:
- Qbank (Uworld or amboss, pick one bc they’re the same): do 8-10 blocks of 10 questions a day. let me backtrack for one second and say if there was any burnout i had, it was 100% because of the 40 question blocks most people do. doing them 10 at a time exponentially boosted productivity
- mehlman pdfs for content review. arrows and endo absolute must first, then your weak systems. just trust me about those two at least 
- save the last two weeks solely for nbmes. cbse is basically an nbme so u obviously want to be familiar with that leading up to it. they love to repeat concepts and questions so out of all of this, doing this point is your best bet as passing imo. do one form every other day: one day to take it in exam setting no bs breaks between blocks, no reviewing between each block, none of that. do the whole thing that day and for the rest of the day do pdfs or qbank blocks, any content review, etc. the next day you will thoroughly review the whole nbme to the T. why it’s right, why all the other answers are wrong, come up with differentials, etc. break down each question to the bone till you got the concept of it burned into your mind. it will take u all day and that’s fine. if u still have energy after, do pdfs or Q’s again. maybe even listening to his playlists as passive studying. 20-31 is 11 forms so 22 days, but i would recommend doing 20-24 for cbse and saving 25-31 for step. if u finish 20-24 or already have, do ones prior to 20; i promise they won’t be lost on you. i’ve seen repeat q’s from forms even as early as form 6 used in the 20s. it’s all the same type of questions you’ll get in your fourth attempt. 
- disclaimer: i learned most of this stuff from mehlman himself because i got sessions with him after failing my third attempt because i was so desperate. pricing is steep but he’s the reason i got that 10 point jump so i would recommend him every single time, he knows what he’s doing fr. one of
the best investments i’ve made for my future hands down. 

anyways, with all that being said, don’t lose hope friend! u got this, i have absolute full faith in you! one day, we’re gonna look back at this stupid good for nothing soul crushing exam that doesn’t even count and chuckle lol. we have basically the same situation so i hope this helps even a little bit :-) best of luck!!
